parallel.requirements: Required a pure Node ESM implementation of argparse-compatible --a, yaml.safe_load, and yaml.dump(default_style='|') with final /output/test14.mjs.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent performed probes and wrote modules while delegating a 14-category adversarial corpus workflow to child agents.
parallel.implementation: Partial implementation libraries were written for scanning, reading, values, numeric conversion, sorting, characters, and errors.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No test14.mjs entry point was delivered; artifact validation listed only library files.
parallel.verification: Parallel attempted broad differential corpus generation, but the workflow was killed before a usable complete aggregate; official evaluator passed 0 of 140.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: Required entry point and integrated safe_load/dump pipeline remained absent despite partial modules.

serial.requirements: Required the same pure Node ESM port with local modules, exact --a behavior, no external dependencies, and /output/test14.mjs.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single agent investigated the executable and wrote local implementation modules without delegation.
serial.implementation: Partial YAML-related libraries were produced, including reader, scanner, pytypes, pyrepr, tokens, chars, errors, and pysort.
serial.integration_and_delivery: No test14.mjs entry point was delivered; artifact validation listed only library files.
serial.verification: Local probing and syntax checks occurred, but official evaluator passed 0 of 140 because the entry point was absent.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The implementation never reached a runnable final program even though several support modules existed.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Recognized the Python task as PyYAML safe_load followed by yaml.dump with default_style='|' and the required --a argument.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Recognized the same prompt, required --a argument, Node ESM, local modules, and final /output/test14.mjs requirement.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference is proven; both ultimately failed delivery by omitting test14.mjs.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Split work between parent-authored implementation modules and a 14-category child corpus workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Kept all investigation and implementation local to the single serial agent with no delegation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel added broad auxiliary corpus ownership; serial used one local implementation path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Corpus children received detailed category prompts and shared /workspace/probe/corpus, with explicit no-/output restriction.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No child brief or cross-agent interface existed; all context stayed inside the parent trajectory.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel created child-context and shared-workspace boundaries; serial had no inter-agent handoff boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Produced partial YAML support modules such as tokens, reader, scanner, chars, and numeric helpers but no entry point.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Produced a similar partial library set including reader, scanner, pytypes, and support modules but no entry point.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both implementation paths were incomplete; module names differed, but both stopped before runnable test14.mjs delivery.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The corpus workflow did not return a usable aggregate result because it was killed with unfinished retrying children.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: No delegated result lifecycle existed; the serial parent alone reached closure with partial files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had an unresolved child workflow lifecycle; serial had only local unfinished work.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote in a shared corpus workspace and hit a concrete _probe.mjs same-file conflict.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no shared child workspace and no cross-agent write conflict.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced shared-state coordination overhead absent from serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel planned differential corpus work, but official evaluation found 0 of 140 samples passing after the missing entry.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed local probing and official evaluation also found 0 of 140 samples passing after the missing entry.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Neither run reached evaluator-aligned acceptance; parallel's verifier workflow was unfinished, while serial had no child verifier.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The 14-agent workflow consumed large budget with repeated stall retries and was killed before integration was complete.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial run spent its budget on local implementation and closed with partial libraries only.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both closed unsuccessfully, but the parallel closure included fan-out budget exhaustion as an added adverse process episode.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is not discordant: both modes failed the current completed evaluation with 0 of 140 samples and solution_passed false. The concrete shared failure is delivery: artifact validation in both modes expected test14.mjs but found only library files. The task-solving difference is process-level: the parallel run added a broad killed child corpus workflow and a shared helper-file collision, while the serial run remained a single local implementation attempt. Those parallel coordination problems were adverse, but they do not explain an outcome difference because the serial control also failed before delivering the entry point.
parallel_contributors: Broad 14-agent corpus fan-out consumed substantial budget and ended killed with unfinished children.
Shared corpus helper name collision forced child-level rerouting and rework.
serial_contributors: Serial stayed local with no delegation but still left the required test14.mjs absent.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both attempts wrote different partial support-module sets but neither assembled a runnable entry point.

The parallel parent launched a broad corpus workflow with 14 live category agents. The workflow state shows repeated stall retries, 1,250,656 tokens, 437 tool calls, status killed, and unfinished children, while the final artifact still lacked the required test14.mjs entry point. This is collective breadth and retry exhaustion, not a single-child scope problem.
candidates.realized_consequence: The corpus workflow remained killed and incomplete after consuming substantial budget, and the required entry/integration step was still absent from the artifact.
candidates.near_match_reason: No one child is the direct overbroad assignment; the adverse episode is the collective 14-agent breadth plus repeated stall retries.

Two live workflow children used the shared /workspace/probe/corpus directory and targeted the same scratch helper name _probe.mjs. One child created it, a second attempted to write the same file, hit the read-before-write guard, then explicitly recognized the file belonged to another agent and switched to uniquely named helpers.
candidates.realized_consequence: The second child had to abandon the shared helper name and spend extra coordination effort switching to uniquely named files in the shared corpus workspace.
candidates.near_match_reason: The broader shared-workspace label is less specific because the concrete episode is a same-path helper collision observed by a live child.
